title: A new proof of the logarithmic Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality for subcritical and critical mass
author: Charles Elbar, Alejandro Fernández-Jiménez, Filippo Santambrogio
work: A Li–Yau and Aronson–Bénilan approach for the Keller–Segel system with critical exponent
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 6.9 (source label 'thm:new_proof_hls'), restated in the introduction as Theorem 1.11: the logarithmic Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality for absolutely continuous measures with finite logarithmic moment and finite entropy, in the subcritical case of mass below eight pi with an explicit constant, and in the critical case of mass exactly eight pi with the corrected inequality containing the factor one minus kappa over two and the logarithmic radius term. The unit is research level because the counted proof is a complete original argument of more than a hundred lines that reproves the inequality by convex-analysis and optimal-transport tools rather than by the classical route: it sets the pointwise inequality between a product and its entropy-weight counterpart, passes to the Euler-Lagrange equation of the entropy functional under the logarithmic kernel, identifies the family of optimisers, and then controls the remaining error terms in the subcritical and the critical mass regimes through the compactness and concentration analysis developed earlier in the article, including the exclusion of Dirac concentrations at critical mass. Establishing a sharp inequality with equality cases through this variational route, and handling the critical exponent where the classical argument loses compactness, is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
